description.narrative: The Urban Infrastructure Project for Bolivia aims at improving access to basic services to the urban poor in Bolivia's major cities through targeted infrastructure investments and the provision of technical assistance to municipalities in the planning, expansion and sustainability of urban service delivery. Project components are: 1: Urban upgrading in La Paz (US$10.4 million, of which US$l0.0 million IDA credit and US$0.4 million in local counterpart financing) Sub-components include: preparation, strengthening community organization and development, and physical infrastructure. 2: Transport in El Alto (US$ 10 million, of which US$10 million IDA credit). Sub-components include: trunk infrastructure development, modernization of public transport services and urban transport management, capacity-building and institutional strengthening, and project implementation. 3: Sanitation in Santa Cruz (US$ 10.0 million, of which US$l0.0 million IDA credit).

The project development objective is to improve the access to basic services to the Urban poor in Bolivia (La Paz, El Alto and Santa Cuz) through targeted infrastructure investments and the provision of technical assistance to municipalities in the planning, expansion and sustainability of urban service delivery.

title.narrative: Reduced rate of groundwater contamination (mg/L) - Santa Cruz

comment.narrative: At the time Component 3 closed, the average concentration was 9.1 g/ml (as reported on August 30, 2012). The indicator did not meet the revised target at the time of closing due to the hydrogeological dynamics of the city's main aquifer. The contamination of thequifer continued given the low sewerage coverage in Santa Cruz (60% at the time of closing). However, according to SAGUAPAC, by the end of 2012 the average concentration of NO3 was 8.9mg/l, and in 2013 it was 8.2 mg/l, almost reaching the target.

comment.narrative: In addition to the effects of the Project, property values have also been positively affected by recent legal reforms in the cadaster valuation (by combining residential and commercial valuations), which elevated property values citywide. Hence, the actual value achieved might not be fully attributable to the Project.

The contamination of thequifer continued given the low sewerage coverage in Santa Cruz (60% at the time of closing). However, according to SAGUAPAC, by the end of 2012 the average concentration of NO3 was 8.9mg/l, and in 2013 it was 8.2 mg/l almost reaching the Project target.
